# Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 1 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** P.Bodmer V / Greek MSS, Proto-Gospel of James 1 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/POX_001_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 1

**1:1** In the records of the twelve tribes of Israel there was a man named Joachim, a man of great wealth. He doubled his offerings before the Lord God, reasoning to himself: "The gift that benefits all the people shall be from my abundance, and my offering shall serve as atonement for the whole people, that I may find forgiveness before the Lord my God."

**1:2** When the great feast day of the Lord arrived, the children of Israel came forward with their offerings. Reuben confronted him, saying: "It is not permitted for you to present your offering before others, since you have produced no offspring in Israel."

**1:3** Joachim was deeply distressed. He consulted the genealogical records of the twelve tribes, saying to himself: "I will examine the records to see whether I am truly the only one who has not fathered children in Israel." He searched and found that every righteous man had indeed produced offspring in Israel. He then recalled the patriarch Abraham, to whom God had granted a son, Isaac, in his final years.

**1:4** Greatly grieved, Joachim withdrew from his wife's presence and went out into the wilderness, where he set up his tent. He fasted there for forty days and forty nights, saying within himself: "I will not return for food or drink until the Lord my God visits me; prayer alone shall be my sustenance."
